author: Bricken et al.
title: Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning
summary: Anthropic's foundational paper applying an L1 sparse autoencoder to the residual stream of a 1-layer transformer and recovering ~15k monosemantic features from GPT-2-scale activations. Establishes feature splitting, automated interpretability, and the dictionary-learning framework for mechanistic interpretability.
why_relevant: Baseline architecture (standard L1 SAE) and training recipe that matryoshka-BatchTopK improves over; also defines the evaluation playbook (feature-specificity, automated interp, ablation) the user will reuse for RFD3 features. Q1.
citation_lines: Section 'Problem Setup', 'Detailed Investigations of Individual Features', 'Global Analysis'

author: Makhzani and Frey
title: k-Sparse Autoencoders
summary: Introduces the TopK activation for autoencoders: keep only the k largest hidden activations per sample, zeroing the rest. Demonstrates better classification and faster training than L1-penalised and denoising autoencoders on MNIST/NORB.
why_relevant: Direct ancestor of TopK and BatchTopK SAEs. Justifies the per-sample sparsity lever that downstream BatchTopK relaxes. Q1.
citation_lines: Sec. 2 (The k-Sparse Autoencoder), Algorithm 1

author: Elhage et al.
title: Toy Models of Superposition
summary: Theoretical and empirical account of how neural networks represent more features than they have dimensions by placing them in superposition. Introduces the feature-sparsity phase diagram and explains polysemanticity via uniform-polytope geometries.
why_relevant: Core motivation for using SAEs at all: if RFD3's residual stream stores structural concepts in superposition, dictionary learning is the natural tool to decompose them. Q1, Q4.
citation_lines: Sec. 2 'Definitions and Motivation', Sec. 3 'Demonstrating Superposition', Fig. 'Phase Diagram'

author: Cunningham et al.
title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models
summary: Shows that sparse autoencoders trained on Pythia residual-stream activations yield features that are substantially more monosemantic than neurons or PCA directions, and that these features are causally implicated in downstream behaviours (e.g., IOI task).
why_relevant: Parallel independent evidence that residual-stream SAEs work; validates the user's choice to target the DiffusionTransformer residual stream rather than MLP neurons. Q3.
citation_lines: Sec. 3 (Taking Features out of Superposition), Sec. 5 (Evaluating Interpretability), Sec. 6 (Case Study: IOI)

author: Templeton et al.
title: Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet
summary: Scales SAEs to Claude-3-Sonnet's middle residual stream and recovers millions of highly abstract, multilingual, multimodal features including concrete behavioural-steering directions. Introduces many of the now-standard SAE feature-quality metrics.
why_relevant: Demonstrates middle-layer residual-stream SAEs scale to frontier models and yield steerable features, which is exactly the regime the user is targeting (block 12 of 18 in RFD3's DiT stack). Q3.
citation_lines: Section 'Sparse Autoencoders', Section 'Assessing Feature Interpretability', Section 'Features as Computational Intermediates'

author: Rajamanoharan et al.
title: Improving Dictionary Learning with Gated Sparse Autoencoders
summary: Introduces Gated SAEs, which decouple the which-direction-to-activate decision from the how-much-to-activate magnitude, fixing the L1-induced shrinkage bias. Matches reconstruction fidelity of L1 SAEs with roughly half the firing features.
why_relevant: A key alternative architecture the user is comparing against. Motivates why sparsity-magnitude decoupling matters and frames why TopK/BatchTopK sidesteps the issue. Q1.
citation_lines: Sec. 3 (Gated SAEs), Eq. 8-10, Fig. 1, Table 1

author: Gao et al.
title: Scaling and Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders
summary: OpenAI's systematic scaling study of TopK SAEs on GPT-2 through GPT-4 residual streams. Derives clean scaling laws in (N, K), introduces feature-quality metrics (downstream-sparsity, probe loss, explanation precision), and shows layer 5/6 of depth is a sweet spot.
why_relevant: Directly motivates the user's choice of block 12/18 (~2/3 depth) for RFD3 and provides the scaling laws that inform dictionary-size sweeps. Canonical reference for TopK. Q1, Q3.
citation_lines: Sec. 2.1 (Setup, layer choice), Sec. 3 (Scaling laws), Eq. 3, Fig. 1, App. F.1

author: Rajamanoharan et al.
title: Jumping Ahead: Improving Reconstruction Fidelity with JumpReLU Sparse Autoencoders
summary: Replaces the ReLU in an SAE with a discontinuous JumpReLU trained with straight-through estimators that directly optimises L0. Achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction-sparsity Pareto on Gemma-2 9B versus TopK and Gated SAEs.
why_relevant: Strong current alternative to BatchTopK; sets the fidelity baseline the user should compare matryoshka-BatchTopK reconstructions against on RFD3 activations. Q1.
citation_lines: Sec. 3 (JumpReLU SAEs), Eq. 4-6, Fig. 2 (Pareto frontier)

author: Bussmann et al.
title: BatchTopK Sparse Autoencoders
summary: Relaxes TopK's per-sample constraint to a batch-level one: pick the top n*k activations across a batch of n samples. Matches JumpReLU fidelity on GPT-2-Small and Gemma-2-2B while allowing exact specification of average L0.
why_relevant: Half of the user's chosen architecture. Justifies why BatchTopK beats TopK on variable-complexity inputs, which matters for protein tokens that range from rigid cores to disordered loops. Q1.
citation_lines: Sec. 3 (BatchTopK SAEs), Eq. 6 (training objective), Eq. 7 (inference threshold), Fig. 1-2

author: Bussmann et al.
title: Learning Multi-Level Features with Matryoshka Sparse Autoencoders
summary: Trains nested dictionaries of increasing size simultaneously; each prefix must reconstruct the input on its own, which forces general features into small prefixes and specific features into larger suffixes. Reduces feature absorption and improves sparse-probing/concept-erasure metrics on Gemma-2-2B.
why_relevant: The other half of the user's chosen architecture. Hierarchical features map naturally onto protein structure (fold class -> secondary structure -> local motif -> atomic detail), making matryoshka a principled fit for RFD3. Q1, Q4.
citation_lines: Sec. 3.1 (Training Objective), Sec. 3.2 (BatchTopK Activation), Sec. 4.3 (Gemma-2-2B), Fig. 1

author: Jumper et al.
title: Highly Accurate Protein Structure Prediction with AlphaFold
summary: Introduces AlphaFold2 with its Evoformer and invariant-point-attention structure module, achieving near-experimental accuracy on CASP14. Establishes the architectural pattern (pair representation, IPA, recycling) that RoseTTAFold and RFdiffusion inherit.
why_relevant: Architectural lineage: RFdiffusion and RFD3 reuse core ideas (pair/single rep, SE(3)-equivariant updates) from AF2; understanding them is needed to interpret what any RFD3 layer is computing. Q2.
citation_lines: Sec. 'Network Architecture', Fig. 3 (Evoformer/Structure Module), Methods 1.7 (IPA)

author: Lin et al.
title: Evolutionary-scale Prediction of Atomic-level Protein Structure with a Language Model
summary: Trains ESM-2 (up to 15B params) and stacks a folding head (ESMFold) to predict atomic-level structure from single sequences with AF2-comparable accuracy and 10x speed. Shows structural information emerges in PLM attention as scale grows.
why_relevant: ESM-2 is the subject of most prior protein-SAE work (InterPLM etc.) and provides the natural baseline for structural-feature discovery the user wants to port to RFD3. Q4.
citation_lines: Sec. 'Language models emergently predict structure', Fig. 2 (scaling), Fig. 4 (ESMFold)

author: Watson et al.
title: De Novo Design of Protein Structure and Function with RFdiffusion
summary: Fine-tunes RoseTTAFold as a denoising diffusion generative model over protein backbones and demonstrates design of binders, symmetric oligomers, enzyme active-site scaffolds, and motif scaffolding, with experimental validation including a picomolar binder. Introduces hotspot and secondary-structure conditioning.
why_relevant: Original RFdiffusion: defines the hotspot, motif/scaffold, and secondary-structure conditioning signals that should appear as features in RFD3's residual stream and that the steerability benchmarks target. Q2, Q4.
citation_lines: Sec. 'RFdiffusion' (architecture), Sec. 'Binder design' (hotspots), Sec. 'Motif scaffolding', Fig. 1, Fig. 4

author: Krishna et al.
title: Generalized Biomolecular Modeling and Design with RoseTTAFold All-Atom
summary: Extends RoseTTAFold to treat arbitrary small molecules, metals, and covalent modifications as atomic graphs alongside residue tokens, and fine-tunes it into RFdiffusionAA for small-molecule-binder design. Establishes the mixed atom/residue tokenisation that RFD3 inherits.
why_relevant: Direct architectural predecessor of RFD3; the mixed atom-and-residue token vocabulary is exactly what the StructureLocalAtomTransformerBlock operates on. Q2.
citation_lines: Sec. 'RFAA architecture', Fig. 1 (tokenisation), Fig. 3 (ligand-binding design)

author: Abramson et al.
title: Accurate Structure Prediction of Biomolecular Interactions with AlphaFold 3
summary: Introduces AlphaFold3 with a diffusion-based structure module operating over token + atom representations, replacing the IPA of AF2. Predicts joint structures of proteins, nucleic acids, small molecules, ions, and modified residues with strong performance on interfaces.
why_relevant: RFD3's DiffusionTransformer is explicitly modeled on the AF3 diffusion module; understanding AF3's token/atom pair streams and local-attention blocks is essential to interpret what block 12 of RFD3 is actually computing. Q2.
citation_lines: Sec. 'Diffusion module', Fig. 1d (diffusion architecture), Fig. 2 (atom/token attention), Methods 3

author: Baker Lab
title: De Novo Design of All-atom Biomolecular Interactions with RFdiffusion3
summary: Preprint introducing RFD3, an atom-level diffusion model with a transformer-based U-Net (downsample, sparse transformer, upsample) that diffuses over atomic coordinates (4 backbone + 10 sidechain + virtual atoms per residue). 10x faster than RFdiffusion2 and validated on DNA binders and cysteine hydrolases.
why_relevant: The exact model the user is studying. Its Section 2 architecture description is the ground truth for what StructureLocalAtomTransformerBlock does and which representation the residual stream carries at block 12. Q2.
citation_lines: Sec. 2 (RFdiffusion3 architecture and training), Fig. 1c (model diagram), Supp. Methods (atom/token attention)

author: Dauparas et al.
title: Robust Deep Learning-based Protein Sequence Design Using ProteinMPNN
summary: A graph neural network that predicts sequence from backbone coordinates with 52.4% native recovery and strong experimental success across monomers, oligomers, and binders. Standard tool for assigning sequences to RFdiffusion backbones.
why_relevant: Downstream evaluator for RFD3 designs, and defines the interface-vs-core residue context the user wants SAE features to encode. Q4.
citation_lines: Sec. 'Model architecture', Fig. 1, Fig. 4 (experimental validation)

author: Dauparas et al.
title: Atomic Context-conditioned Protein Sequence Design Using LigandMPNN
summary: Extends ProteinMPNN with explicit non-protein atomic context (small molecules, nucleotides, metals), lifting interface native sequence recovery from ~50% to 63% (small molecule), 50% (nucleotide), and 77% (metal). Generates sidechain conformations jointly.
why_relevant: Defines the exact feature categories the user wants to probe for in RFD3: pocket residues, nucleic-acid interface residues, and metal coordinators. Q4.
citation_lines: Sec. 'Model architecture', Table 1 (sequence recovery), Fig. 2 (ligand-conditioned design)

author: Kabsch and Sander
title: Dictionary of Protein Secondary Structure
summary: Canonical algorithm (DSSP) for assigning protein secondary structure from atomic coordinates using an electrostatic hydrogen-bond energy with a -0.5 kcal/mol cutoff. Defines alpha/3-10/pi helix, beta sheet/bridge, turn, and bend classes still used today.
why_relevant: Provides the ground-truth labels for probing SAE features for alpha-helix, beta-strand, and turn content, and the target for the 'steer helix %' benchmark. Q4.
citation_lines: Sec. 'Hydrogen Bond Definition', Sec. 'Pattern Recognition', Table I (H-bond energy), Table III (SS classes)

author: Le Guilloux et al.
title: Fpocket: An Open Source Platform for Ligand Pocket Detection
summary: Voronoi-tessellation-based pocket detector using alpha spheres to identify and score putative ligand-binding cavities on protein surfaces. Detects 94%/92% of known pockets within the top-3 predictions on holo/apo sets.
why_relevant: Programmatic source of pocket-residue labels for evaluating whether any SAE feature fires on ligand-pocket residues in RFD3. Q4.
citation_lines: Sec. 'Implementation', Sec. 'Pocket detection algorithm', Table 2 (detection rate)

author: Simon and Zou
title: InterPLM: Discovering Interpretable Features in Protein Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
summary: Trains SAEs on ESM-2 residual streams and finds up to 2,548 interpretable features per layer aligning with 143 Swiss-Prot biological concepts (binding sites, motifs, domains), plus novel families with no known annotations. Ships InterPLM.ai for visualisation and shows targeted sequence-steering.
why_relevant: Most directly analogous prior work: same SAE toolkit, protein substrate, and concept ontology the user wants to apply to RFD3 structural activations. Establishes expected feature yield. Q4.
citation_lines: Sec. 'Training sparse autoencoders on ESM-2', Sec. 'Concept alignment', Fig. 2 (feature-concept correspondence), Fig. 5 (steering)

author: Adams et al.
title: From Mechanistic Interpretability to Mechanistic Biology: Training, Evaluating, and Interpreting Sparse Autoencoders on Protein Language Models
summary: Trains SAEs and transcoders on ESM-2 residual streams and protein-level mean embeddings, identifies features linked to Gene Ontology terms, and uses linear probes on SAE features to recover known sequence determinants of thermostability and subcellular localisation.
why_relevant: Validates linear-probing SAE features for biologically meaningful downstream predictions, which the user can adopt for RFD3 feature evaluation (e.g., probing helix%, SASA, hotspot flag). Q4.
citation_lines: Sec. 3 (SAE training setup), Sec. 4 (GO-term alignment), Sec. 5 (linear probing for thermostability/localization)

author: Yang et al.
title: Towards Interpretable Protein Structure Prediction with Sparse Autoencoders
summary: Scales Matryoshka and TopK SAEs to ESM2-3B (the ESMFold backbone), recovers 233 Swiss-Prot concepts with F1 > 0.5, and demonstrates causal steering: activating an SAE feature raises ESMFold's predicted total SASA by 31.5% at fixed sequence.
why_relevant: The closest existing proof-of-concept for matryoshka SAEs on a protein structure model with successful structural steering; a template for the RFD3 steerability benchmarks. Q1, Q4.
citation_lines: Sec. 2.2 (Matryoshka SAEs), Sec. 4.1 (Swiss-Prot Concept Discovery), Sec. 5.1 (SAE Feature Steering on ESMFold), App. E, App. H
